日文.首段: 身延山（みのぶさん）は山梨県南巨摩郡の身延町と早川町の境にある山である。標高1,153m。また同地にある日蓮宗総本山久遠寺の山号でもあり、日本仏教三大霊山の一つという別名としてもよく用いられる。

章节.概要:
日蓮宗の開祖日蓮聖人が、身延山の草庵に居を定めたのは、文永11年（1274年）6月17日（新暦7月21日）。山麓の標高400m付近に日蓮宗総本山である身延山久遠寺があり、山頂にも日蓮が父母を偲んで建立したと言われる奥之院思親閣がある。身延山の参拝客のほか、頂上からの眺望がよいため観光客も多く訪れる。

身延山の周辺には鷹取山（1,036m）、七面山（1,982m）などの山があり、いずれも日蓮宗の修行の場でもある。
山頂へはロープウェイで7分程度で登れる。山頂部には奥之院と3つの展望台が設置されており、東と南側展望台からは富士山がよく見え、天候がよければ駿河湾、伊豆半島を見晴らすことができる。特に3月中旬および10月上旬には、富士山山頂から日が昇るダイヤモンド富士が見られるため、前後数日の早朝は観望や写真撮影の客で賑わう。北側展望台からは南アルプスや甲府盆地、七面山や早川町の町並みが眺望できる。
山腹には雑木林が分布するほか、杉が植林されている。周辺には『甲州盆歌』に歌われたナンテンが見られ、山頂にはカタクリも自生する。「仏法僧（ブッポウソウ）」と鳴くことで知られるコノハズクや、ニホンカモシカ、イノシシ、ツキノワグマなどが生息する。
章节.登山: 久遠寺境内付近から標高差約760m、50丁の参道があり、東側の尾根を回って登れ、徒歩で約2時間30分の道のりである。途中の25丁にある三光堂までは自動車も入れるよう舗装されているが、一般客は自動車では進入できない。この参道入り口をやや下ると身延山ロープウェイの久遠寺駅があり、山頂まで約7分で到達できる。また、他のルートとして、早川町方面からの登山道があり、身延町の飛び地である七面山方面に通じている。この参道の途中からは山の南西を巡って日蓮の草庵のあった西谷方面に下山できる。
章节.身延山ロープウェイ:
身延山ロープウェイは身延山の山麓と山頂を結ぶ三線交走式の索道（ロープウェイ）である。現在富士急行の持分法適用会社となっている身延登山鉄道により建設され、1962年（昭和37年）12月27日に事業許可を受け、1963年（昭和38年）8月23日に開業した。当初、身延山山頂へはケーブルカーによる輸送を計画し工事が進められたが、軟弱な地盤や法面の崩落などによりこれを断念し、ロープウェイに変更された経緯がある（「登山鉄道」の社名はその名残である）。山麓の久遠寺駅、山頂の奥之院駅の2駅間の斜長1,665m、標高差763mを約7分で運行する。標高差763mは関東一である。平常時は20分おき、繁忙期には増発や運転時間延長もある。
1981年（昭和56年）に2代目ゴンドラとして日本ケーブル/武庫川車両により製造された定員45名のもの2両が用いられていた（それぞれ「たちばな号」「ぼたん号」と名づけられていた）。2011年（平成23年）7月に搬器・駅などがJR九州や両備グループの各車両や富士急行の「富士登山電車」などのデザインを手がけた水戸岡鋭治によってリニューアルされた。
2代目導入から40年が経過することから2021年（令和3年）1月31日を以て運行を一時休止し、3代目ゴンドラに置き換えることが発表された。新ゴンドラでの運用は2月23日より開始される。2021年2月23日から運用されるゴンドラ2両は「知恩号」「報恩号」と名づけられた。

1号車「知恩号」（定員41名）外装は朱色で内天井には久遠寺天井画の墨龍が描かれている。
2号車「報恩号」（定員41名）外装は藍色で内天井には七面山敬慎院の天井模様が描かれている。
章节.身延テレビ・FM中継放送所:
山頂付近には、峡南地域のテレビジョン・FMラジオ放送の中核中継局が設けられている。アナログVHF中継局の出力は下部中継局のほうが大きいが、地形的な要因もあり、ここが中核局として扱われている。
甲府親局もそうだが、山梨県は山がちで、電波が飛びにくい地形といわれているため、通常アナログUHF局映像出力の1割とされるデジタルテレビジョン放送の出力は、その6分の1と高めに設定された。

章节.地上アナログテレビジョン放送（廃止）:
VHF各局のみ甲府送信所と同一チャンネルで送信している。
全局2011年7月24日の停波をもって廃止。
章节.FMラジオ放送:
身延山から発射されているFM波は、旧身延町住民の強い要望により、1968年（昭和43年）に開局された。
エフエム富士については、新聞によっては中継局名が「静岡」とされているものもある。

英文.首段: Mount Minobu (みのぶさん) is a mountain on the border between Minobu Town and Hayakawa Town in Minamikoma District, Yamanashi Prefecture. Its elevation is 1,153 m. It is also the mountain name (sangō) of Kuonji, the head temple of the Nichiren sect located there, and is often used as an alternative name meaning one of the three great sacred mountains of Japanese Buddhism.

章节.Overview:
It was on June 17, 1274 (Bun'ei 11) (July 21 in the new calendar) that Saint Nichiren, founder of the Nichiren sect, settled in a grass hut on Mount Minobu. Near an elevation of 400 m at the foot of the mountain is Minobusan Kuonji, the head temple of the Nichiren sect, and at the summit there is the Okunoin Shishinkaku, said to have been built by Nichiren in memory of his parents. Besides worshippers visiting Mount Minobu, many tourists also come because of the fine view from the summit.

Around Mount Minobu are mountains such as Mt. Takatori (1,036 m) and Mt. Shichimen (1,982 m), all of which are also places of Nichiren sect ascetic practice.
The summit can be reached in about 7 minutes by ropeway. At the summit are the Okunoin and three observation decks; from the east and south decks, Mount Fuji can be seen well, and in good weather Suruga Bay and the Izu Peninsula can be viewed. Especially in mid-March and early October, "Diamond Fuji"—the sun rising from the summit of Mount Fuji—can be seen, so in the early mornings for several days around those times the area is crowded with people viewing and photographing it. From the north deck, the Southern Alps, the Kofu Basin, and the townscapes of Mt. Shichimen and Hayakawa Town can be viewed.
On the slopes are distributed coppice forests, and cedars have been planted. In the surroundings, nanten (nandina) sung about in the "Koshu Bon-uta" can be seen, and dogtooth violets (katakuri) also grow wild at the summit. It is inhabited by the collared scops owl, known for its call "buppōsō," as well as the Japanese serow, wild boar, and Asian black bear.

英文.全文:
Mount Minobu (みのぶさん) is a mountain on the border between Minobu Town and Hayakawa Town in Minamikoma District, Yamanashi Prefecture. Its elevation is 1,153 m. It is also the mountain name (sangō) of Kuonji, the head temple of the Nichiren sect located there, and is often used as an alternative name meaning one of the three great sacred mountains of Japanese Buddhism.

== Overview ==

It was on June 17, 1274 (Bun'ei 11) (July 21 in the new calendar) that Saint Nichiren, founder of the Nichiren sect, settled in a grass hut on Mount Minobu. Near an elevation of 400 m at the foot of the mountain is Minobusan Kuonji, the head temple of the Nichiren sect, and at the summit there is the Okunoin Shishinkaku, said to have been built by Nichiren in memory of his parents. Besides worshippers visiting Mount Minobu, many tourists also come because of the fine view from the summit.

Around Mount Minobu are mountains such as Mt. Takatori (1,036 m) and Mt. Shichimen (1,982 m), all of which are also places of Nichiren sect ascetic practice.
The summit can be reached in about 7 minutes by ropeway. At the summit are the Okunoin and three observation decks; from the east and south decks, Mount Fuji can be seen well, and in good weather Suruga Bay and the Izu Peninsula can be viewed. Especially in mid-March and early October, "Diamond Fuji"—the sun rising from the summit of Mount Fuji—can be seen, so in the early mornings for several days around those times the area is crowded with people viewing and photographing it. From the north deck, the Southern Alps, the Kofu Basin, and the townscapes of Mt. Shichimen and Hayakawa Town can be viewed.
On the slopes are distributed coppice forests, and cedars have been planted. In the surroundings, nanten (nandina) sung about in the "Koshu Bon-uta" can be seen, and dogtooth violets (katakuri) also grow wild at the summit. It is inhabited by the collared scops owl, known for its call "buppōsō," as well as the Japanese serow, wild boar, and Asian black bear.

== Mountaineering ==

From near the Kuonji temple grounds there is a 50-chō pilgrimage path with an elevation difference of about 760 m, which can be climbed by going around the eastern ridge, a route of about 2 hours 30 minutes on foot. Up to Sankōdō at the 25th chō, the path is paved so that cars can enter, but ordinary visitors cannot enter by car. A little below the entrance to this pilgrimage path is the Kuonji Station of the Minobusan Ropeway, from which the summit can be reached in about 7 minutes. Another route is a climbing trail from the Hayakawa Town side, which leads toward Mt. Shichimen, an exclave of Minobu Town. From partway along this pilgrimage path one can descend around the southwest of the mountain toward Nishidani, where Nichiren's grass hut was located.

== Minobusan Ropeway ==

The Minobusan Ropeway is a three-line reversible aerial tramway (ropeway) connecting the foot and summit of Mount Minobu. It was built by Minobu Tozan Railway, now an equity-method affiliate of Fuji Kyuko, which received a business license on December 27, 1962 (Showa 37) and opened on August 23, 1963 (Showa 38). Initially, transport to the summit of Mount Minobu was planned by funicular (cable car) and construction proceeded, but this was abandoned due to soft ground and slope collapse, and it was changed to a ropeway (the company name "Tozan Railway" [mountain-climbing railway] is a remnant of this). It operates between two stations—Kuonji Station at the foot and Okunoin Station at the summit—over a slope length of 1,665 m and an elevation difference of 763 m in about 7 minutes. The elevation difference of 763 m is the largest in the Kanto region. Normally it runs every 20 minutes, and during busy periods there are additional services and extended operating hours.
In 1981 (Showa 56), two second-generation gondolas with a capacity of 45 people, manufactured by Nippon Cable/Mukogawa Sharyo, were used (they were named "Tachibana" and "Botan" respectively). In July 2011 (Heisei 23), the cars, stations, etc. were renewed by Eiji Mitooka, who designed JR Kyushu and Ryobi Group cars and Fuji Kyuko's "Fuji Tozan Train," among others.
As 40 years had passed since the introduction of the second generation, it was announced that operation would be temporarily suspended as of January 31, 2021 (Reiwa 3) and replaced with third-generation gondolas. Operation with the new gondolas begins on February 23. The two gondolas placed in service from February 23, 2021 were named "Chion" and "Hōon."

Car 1 "Chion" (capacity 41) has a vermilion exterior, and on the inner ceiling is painted the ink dragon of the ceiling painting of Kuonji.
Car 2 "Hōon" (capacity 41) has an indigo exterior, and on the inner ceiling is painted the ceiling pattern of Keishinin on Mt. Shichimen.

== Minobu TV/FM Relay Broadcasting Station ==

Near the summit, a core relay station for television and FM radio broadcasting in the Kanan region is established. For the analog VHF relay station, the output of the lower relay stations is larger, but because of topographical factors, this one is treated as the core station.
As with the Kofu main station, Yamanashi Prefecture is mountainous and is said to be terrain where radio waves do not travel easily, so the output of digital television broadcasting, normally set at one-tenth of the video output of an analog UHF station, was set higher, at one-sixth of that.
